rules.rule:
This file REPLACES the root layout when it renders, so it has no i18n provider, no Tailwind layer and no fonts. The things a reviewer would normally flag here are all deliberate:

- Inline `style` attributes and hard-coded hex colours are REQUIRED. There is no stylesheet at this point. Do not ask for classes or tokens.
- The bilingual copy is hard-coded French and Arabic on purpose. Do not ask for `useTranslations` or any next-intl hook — calling one here throws, because the provider is gone.
- It supplies its own `<html>` and `<body>`. That is correct, not a duplication.

What IS worth flagging: any import of next-intl or of a component that transitively uses it; any reliance on a CSS class; and the error-boundary prop. Next 16 renamed it to `retry`. `reset` still compiles but only re-renders the failed payload instead of re-fetching it, so a silent downgrade from `retry` to `reset` is a real defect.

`sections` and `exercises` are DENORMALISED from the markdown and shown to students as fact. They must be re-derived, never estimated or carried over.

Re-derive by running the real loader (`loadCourseDoc`) and comparing `views.length` and the sum of `view.checkpoints` against the row. `test:course` fails on drift, so a wrong number here is a broken build — but the reason it drifts is the part a reviewer must catch.

`sections` moves for reasons that are NOT edits to the prose. `isLight` in `lib/courseDoc.ts` calls a `##` heavy at more than sixty lines OR more than forty formulas, and cuts a heavy one at its `###`. Repairing delimiters in a chapter — converting `\(…\)` to `$…$`, which `remark-math` can actually parse — made the formula counter see maths that was already there and repaginated three chapters (15→16, 25→27, 7→9) without a word of content changing. So: if a PR touches course markdown at all, even only its delimiters, ask whether these numbers were re-derived.

Also flag any new row whose `filieres` list, `branch` or `n` contradicts the chapter's place in the programme, and any Arabic field (`titleAr`, `descriptionAr`) left as a copy of the French.

Course content for students sitting the Moroccan 2ème Bac. Wrong mathematics here teaches a falsehood to someone being examined on it.

## The two trees must stay identical
`critique/course/` is THE SOURCE; `content/course/` is the copy the app serves. Every edit must land in BOTH, byte for byte. Editing only the served copy means the next sync silently deletes the work. The single exception is `04-fonctions-logarithmiques.md`, which exists only in `content/` because it was migrated from JSX — an allowlist of exactly one, not a licence to add files to `content/` alone.

## Delimiters are not cosmetic
The pipeline is `remark-math`, which parses ONLY `$…$` and `$$…$$`. It does NOT parse `\(…\)` or `\[…\]` — those become plain text, markdown eats the backslashes, and the student is shown literal TeX. Flag any `\(`, `\)`, `\[` or `\]` used as a math delimiter. Note `\[` and `\]` are legitimate INSIDE math (`\sqrt[n]{x}`, `\left[`), so judge by position.

Flag `\\` inside inline math: in KaTeX `\\` is a line break, so `$b' \\mid a'$` renders as `b′` then a break then the letters `mid`. It parses without error, which is exactly why no checker sees it.

## The corpus carries OCR damage, so read the mathematics, not just the syntax
These chapters were extracted from a PDF and the extraction corrupted real mathematics. A formula that RENDERS is not therefore CORRECT. Known classes, all of which have occurred here:
- a derivative read as a square (`y'` → `y²`), or a prime dropped from a section title so a second-order section is labelled first-order;
- the independent variable replaced by the dependent one (`e^{3y}` where `e^{3x}` is meant);
- `*` misread as a letter or digit — `\mathbb{R}_+^*` appearing as `\mathbb{R}_+^n` or `^r`, `\mathbb{R}^3` as `\mathbb{R}^1`;
- a root's index overwritten (`\sqrt[n]{a^p}` → `\sqrt[a^p]`);
- a whole proposition left false while rendering perfectly.

When a stated rule, proposition or worked answer is checkable, CHECK IT, and check it against the lines around it — the neighbouring statement or the exercise below usually pins the intended form.

## Nothing invented
Where the original is unrecoverable, say so and leave it. Do NOT write a plausible replacement exercise, a reconstructed algebraic step, or a renumbered sequence that the document does not determine. An invented question is worse than a visibly broken one, because nothing marks it as untrustworthy. Flag any edit that supplies content the source cannot justify.

## Structure
Do not change the number of `##` headings or `> **Application**` blocks without saying so — `lib/courseCatalog.ts` denormalises both and `test:course` compares them. Never touch a `## Auto-évaluation` section or a ```geogebra block casually; the first is the product's only assessment, the second must stay valid JSON.

Migrations are applied by hand against a live project holding real students' work. There is no rollback.

## Merge, do not overwrite
Writes arrive from several devices belonging to one student. The rule this schema settled on is union-and-maximum for anything that only grows, and date-decides for anything that represents the CURRENT attempt. Flag any trigger or upsert that replaces an array wholesale, or that makes `tried` / `verdict` / `draft` monotonic — those three are cleared deliberately by « Réessayer », and treating them as monotonic hands the student back the wrong answer they just walked away from.

## Never trust a client clock
`updated_at` arrives from the student's browser. Any comparison or `greatest()` on it must clamp first — `least(coalesce(new.updated_at, now()), now())`. Without the clamp, one device with its clock set to a future year pins the row's timestamp there and every correctly-dated write afterwards is discarded, from every device, silently and permanently.

## Identity fields fill gaps, they never blank them
On conflict, use `coalesce(excluded.x, table.x)`, not `excluded.x`. A bare overwrite lets a provider that has stopped returning a field erase the value that was right.

## Triggers that fire once are not repairs
`after insert on auth.users` runs once in an account's lifetime. Any logic that must survive a row being recreated later needs `insert or update`, plus a backfill for the rows already in the bad state. Flag a migration that adds a one-shot trigger and calls it a fix.

## Security
- RLS on every table, and a policy on each — except where the ABSENCE of a policy is the protection; if so, the file must say so.
- `on delete cascade` to `auth.users`, or deleting an account leaves its rows behind.
- `security definer` only where the function genuinely needs to read past RLS, and always with `set search_path`. Flag it where it buys nothing — it is a surface, not a default.

## Say what needs a human
If the migration only takes effect once someone flips a setting in the Supabase dashboard, the file must say so in its header, and nothing elsewhere may assert the protection as already true.

These are the project's verifiers. A check that CANNOT FAIL is worse than no check, because it buys confidence without testing anything. Review them for that first, before style.

## The three shapes that have all occurred here
1. **The mute oracle** — the assertion runs but its result is true whatever happens: `ok(true, …)`, a loop over an array that is empty when the feature is deleted, `!(await x.isVisible().catch(() => false))` which is equally true when the element is missing, or a bare `fetch()` of a gated route that follows the proxy's redirect and reports `/signin`'s 200.
2. **The check that stopped running** — silence read as success: a `catch {}` around a parse, or credentials resolved from `.env.local` only so the whole live half is skipped in CI. Flag any new check that can be skipped without saying so by name.
3. **The check that measures something else** — greps a comment rather than the behaviour, tests that a directory exists rather than what is in it, or asserts on page SOURCE. next-intl ships the ENTIRE message namespace to every page, so `html.includes(someMessage)` passes on any route, including a 404. Assert on rendered elements.

## Rules this repo has adopted
- **Never write a count down.** Each script prints its own (`N of M checks ran`). Three counts were recorded as fact in prose and all three were stale. Flag any hard-coded total in a message, a comment, or a doc.
- **A repair must be proven by injection.** If a PR fixes a verifier, ask which fault was reinserted to show it going red. "It passes now" is not evidence.
- **FIXED must mean tested.** A finding absent from this run is not fixed if its check never executed. Flag state handling that conflates the two.
- Never weaken or delete a check to make it pass.

When a check fires, the fix is the code, not the check — unless the check is measuring the wrong thing, and then the fix must come with the injection proving it still catches the real fault.

Changes here move indexing signals that are invisible in page source. `alternateLinks` controls the `Link: rel="alternate" hreflang` RESPONSE HEADERS next-intl emits from the proxy on every route in both locales; Google honours them like head tags. It must follow `NEXT_PUBLIC_ALLOW_INDEXING` together with the five other signals listed in `lib/publicPaths.ts`. Flag any change that switches it independently.

`localePrefix: 'as-needed'` means French is unprefixed and Arabic lives under `/ar`. Anything that names a URL to a crawler — sitemap, canonical, hreflang, the robots disallow list — needs that same transformation. A rule written without the prefix (`Disallow: /home`) does NOT cover `/ar/home`; robots.txt matching is literal prefix.

Tag Moroccan Arabic as `ar-MA`, never `ary`: CSS `:lang(ar)` matches `ar-MA` and does not match `ary`, so the Arabic typography guard would be escaped silently.

## Never read device state during render
`localStorage` does not exist on the server. Computing anything from it inline makes the server send one value and the browser's first render another, and React throws away the server markup for that subtree. Read it in an effect and render the zero state on BOTH sides. Flag every `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, `window` or `document` access reachable during the first render pass — including inside a `useState` initialiser. `typeof window !== 'undefined' && localStorage.getItem(...)` in render is the exact bug, not the fix for it.

Note the corollary: `useEffect` bodies that call `setState` to hydrate device state are REQUIRED here and are the reason this repo carries `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` warnings. Do not ask for those to be removed; do flag one that reads no device state and could be derived instead.

## A value carried on one side must survive the trip to the other
This has now been the shape of several real defects: a field read correctly in one place and silently dropped on the way to another. A checkpoint's change-time erased by a reader that rebuilt the object without it; a Google display name read to draw the header and omitted from the row that stores it. When reviewing an object literal that is written to storage, sent to the database, or merged, check it against the type it claims to be and flag every field the literal does not carry.

## Whose work is this?
Students share machines. Any write to a device store must belong to the account that owns the device now, not the one that owned it when the tab was opened. Flag a push that reads its payload at flush time rather than capturing it when queued, and any store write on a path that cannot tell whether the device has changed hands.

## Dates
Compare instants, never timestamp strings. PostgREST renders `+00:00` and JS `toISOString()` renders `Z`; inside the same second every digit sorts below `Z`, and a quoted date sorts above every digit. Both of those have already produced a comparison that was wrong every single time. Use `Date.parse` and handle the unparseable case explicitly.

## This product refuses three things
- **No ranking, league or leaderboard.** Progress is compared to the student's own previous window, never to another student.
- **Nothing invented.** No fabricated testimonial, review count, duration, rating or recommendation. Every figure shown must derive from the content or the reader's own device. If the data does not exist, the feature does not ship — an honest count beats an estimate.
- **No auto-graded mathematics.** The self-assessment asks the chapter's own items and the READER judges. Flag any correct-answer field, any ratio taken over correctness, any verdict the machine decides. One deliberate exception exists — the landing page's single hand-authored preview problem, stored and counted nowhere — and both verifier scripts carry a comment saying so.
